description: 10 real production scenarios for insurance AI agents.

scenarios.name: Small claim auto-approved — low fraud score
scenarios.narrative: Claims processing agent handles a $1,800 auto glass claim. Fraud score is 0.12. Claim is below the $2,500 auto-approve threshold.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: AGR enables straight-through processing for low-risk claims. $1,800 glass claims are approved in milliseconds — no adjuster needed, no queue. This is how you improve NPS.

scenarios.name: High-value claim with fraud score routed to SIU
scenarios.narrative: Claims agent processes a $45,000 water damage claim. Fraud score is 0.82 based on claim pattern analysis. Routed to Special Investigations Unit.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Insurance fraud costs the industry $80B annually. AGR catches high-risk claims before payment and routes them to SIU — automatically, consistently, with full audit trail.

scenarios.name: Policy cancellation blocked — insufficient notice period
scenarios.narrative: Policy management agent cancels a homeowners policy with 15 days notice. State insurance code requires minimum 30 days written notice.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Cancelling a policy without proper notice is a state insurance code violation. AGR enforces the notice period — the agent cannot accidentally generate a regulatory complaint.

scenarios.name: Premium increase blocked — exceeds California cap
scenarios.narrative: Pricing agent applies a 30% rate increase to a California auto policy. California Proposition 103 limits increases to 25% without prior DOI approval.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: California Prop 103 violations trigger DOI enforcement and restitution to policyholders. AGR enforces state-specific rate caps as Cedar policies — one rule per state, updated without code changes.

scenarios.name: New rate filing blocked — actuary sign-off missing
scenarios.narrative: Product management agent attempts to file new rates for a commercial property product. Actuarial sign-off is required before any rate filing.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Rate filings without actuarial certification are rejected by state DOIs and expose the company to inadequate rate risk. AGR blocks the filing at the source.

scenarios.name: Health record access blocked — no policyholder consent
scenarios.narrative: Underwriting agent attempts to retrieve medical records for a life insurance application. HIPAA requires explicit authorization from the applicant.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Accessing medical records without HIPAA authorization is a federal violation. AGR checks consent before any medical data is retrieved — regardless of which agent requests it.

scenarios.name: Catastrophic event settlement requires reinsurance confirmation
scenarios.narrative: Claims agent attempts to begin settling a wildfire CAT event with estimated total loss of $12M. Reinsurance recovery must be confirmed before settlement begins.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Settling a $12M CAT event before reinsurance confirmation could exceed the company's net retention. AGR blocks premature settlement — protecting the company's solvency.

scenarios.name: Life policy lapse blocked — lapse notice not sent
scenarios.narrative: Policy administration agent marks a life insurance policy as lapsed due to premium non-payment. State law requires a lapse notice to be sent and acknowledged first.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Lapsing a life policy without notice exposes the carrier to bad faith litigation. AGR makes the lapse notice a mandatory gate — the agent cannot skip it.

scenarios.name: Large settlement offer requires dual approval
scenarios.narrative: Claims agent generates a $250,000 bodily injury settlement offer. Offers above $100,000 require senior claims manager and legal counsel review.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: A $250,000 settlement offer without legal review can trigger bad faith claims if inadequate or overpay if excessive. AGR routes it for dual approval before the offer is communicated.

scenarios.name: Underwriting decision blocked — used protected class attributes
scenarios.narrative: AI underwriting agent makes a denial decision based on a model that included race and marital status as input features. ECOA and state law prohibit using protected class attributes.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: AI underwriting using protected class proxies violates ECOA and triggers disparate impact liability. AGR blocks the decision before it reaches the applicant — this is the only way to govern AI fairly.
